page: Amazon Web Services i8g.48xlarge is a storage-optimized server built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores using the ARM64 architecture, powered by AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processors running at 2.8 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 45,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and network connectivity is supported by a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core and memory performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test scored 314,891.93, placing it in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is also in the top tier, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 21,337.95 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 411.91 GB/sec. In database operations, the server achieved a top-tier PassMark database score of 47,012.32 and processed 349.81 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,658.0, and LLM inference prompt processing for a small 135M model is weak at 224.17 tokens/sec.

The server offers high resource density, combining massive local NVMe storage with a high physical core count on energy-efficient ARM architecture. This hardware profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high-throughput local storage and parallel processing without the overhead of hyperthreading. Appropriate workloads include large-scale databases, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data decompression.
